statement: Let $A,B,C$ be points with position vectors $\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathbf{c}$, and let $G$ be the centroid of triangle $ABC$ so that $\mathbf{g}=\tfrac13(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{c})$. Show that $GA^{2}+GB^{2}+GC^{2}=\tfrac13(AB^{2}+BC^{2}+CA^{2})$.
solution: $GA^{2}+GB^{2}+GC^{2}=|\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{g}|^{2}+|\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{g}|^{2}+|\mathbf{c}-\mathbf{g}|^{2}$. Since $\mathbf{g}=\tfrac13(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{c})$, expanding gives $\tfrac13(|\mathbf{a}|^{2}+|\mathbf{b}|^{2}+|\mathbf{c}|^{2})-\tfrac23(\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{c}+\mathbf{c}\cdot\mathbf{a})$. Meanwhile $AB^{2}+BC^{2}+CA^{2}=2(|\mathbf{a}|^{2}+|\mathbf{b}|^{2}+|\mathbf{c}|^{2})-2(\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{c}+\mathbf{c}\cdot\mathbf{a})$. Dividing this by $3$ gives exactly the expression above, so the identity holds.
hints: Write each squared distance from the centroid.
Compare with the expanded form of $AB^{2}+BC^{2}+CA^{2}$.
